title: The Code of Hammurabi: Law, Status, and Evidence
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
The monument commonly called the Code of Hammurabi was produced in the eighteenth century BCE and later found at Susa. Its long inscription contains a prologue, hundreds of legal judgments, and an epilogue. The judgments often use a conditional form: if a specified event occurs, then a stated consequence follows. The collection addresses property, debt, trade, family, labor, injury, and professional responsibility. It is extensive, but it is not a modern statute book organized around universal rights.

The famous formula “an eye for an eye” can suggest proportional retaliation: a response should correspond to an injury rather than expand into unlimited revenge. But proportionality did not create equality before the law. Consequences varied with the legal status and gender of the people involved. Bodily retaliation in one status relationship could become monetary compensation in another. The text made social hierarchy legible as well as regulated conflict within it.

The monument also performed political and religious work. Above the inscription, Hammurabi faces Shamash, a deity associated with justice. The image and prologue present the king as authorized to establish order. Public visibility could advertise royal justice, but visibility is not the same as universal literacy, equal access, or independent enforcement. A ruler's monument is both legal evidence and a claim about legitimate rule.

Finally, historians must distinguish prescribed norms from everyday practice. A written judgment tells us what an authoritative text represented as proper; by itself it does not show how often officials applied it, negotiated around it, or ignored it. Other contracts, letters, court records, and archaeological evidence are needed. The monument is invaluable not because it gives a transparent photograph of Babylonian life, but because careful comparison lets us ask how law, status, economy, and kingship were connected.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: The monument proves that all Babylonian residents had equal rights.

options.label: B
options.text: The text must be read as legal judgments, social hierarchy, royal representation, and incomplete evidence of practice.

options.label: C
options.text: Every written judgment was always enforced exactly as written.

options.label: D
options.text: Its only subject was violent crime.

questions.answer: 正解：B。本文は法的判断、身分秩序、王権の表象、規範と実務の史料的差を扱います。Aは身分差、Cは規範と運用、Dは対象範囲について本文に反します。

questions.prompt: What does the frequent if–then form reveal about the legal text?

options.label: A
options.text: It is largely a collection linking specified situations to stated consequences rather than a uniform declaration of abstract universal rights.

options.label: B
options.text: It lists rights without referring to events or consequences.

options.label: C
options.text: It records only religious prayers and no legal judgments.

options.label: D
options.text: It guarantees that every case was handled identically in practice.

questions.answer: 正解：A。具体的条件と帰結を結ぶ個別判断の集積であり、普遍的権利を一律に体系化した現代法令集ではありません。B・Cは形式と内容、Dは規範と実務を誤ります。

questions.prompt: The phrase “performed political work” in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: physically repaired a government building

options.label: B
options.text: helped construct and display a claim to authority

options.label: C
options.text: secretly abolished the monarchy

options.label: D
options.text: measured the literacy rate

questions.answer: 正解：B。ここでperformedは、王の権威を構築・提示・正当化する機能を果たしたという意味です。Aは物理的作業への誤読、C・Dは本文にありません。

questions.prompt: Why did proportional retaliation not amount to equality before the law?

options.label: A
options.text: The consequence for the same kind of injury could change with the legal status and gender of the people involved.

options.label: B
options.text: Every injury received exactly the same consequence regardless of status.

options.label: C
options.text: The text prohibited both bodily retaliation and monetary compensation.

options.label: D
options.text: Proportionality applied only to trade and never to injury.

questions.answer: 正解：A。同じ傷害でも当事者の身分・性別によって身体的報復か金銭賠償かが変わり、結果は万人に同一ではありません。B～Dは第2段落と矛盾します。

questions.prompt: How does the image of Hammurabi facing Shamash support a claim of legal legitimacy?

options.label: A
options.text: It presents the king's establishment of order as authorized by a deity associated with justice, not merely as a personal command.

options.label: B
options.text: It proves that every resident could read the entire inscription.

options.label: C
options.text: It separates royal rule completely from religion and justice.

options.label: D
options.text: It shows an independent court overruling the king.

questions.answer: 正解：A。正義に結び付く神の前に王を置き、王の秩序形成を神的権威に支えられたものとして提示します。Bは可視性と識字、C・Dは図像の意味を誤ります。

questions.prompt: Which inference is best supported by the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Public display guarantees universal comprehension.

options.label: B
options.text: A normative text is identical to a record of every actual decision.

options.label: C
options.text: The collection regulates economic and domestic matters as well as injuries.

options.label: D
options.text: Social status never changed a consequence.

questions.answer: 正解：C。財産、債務、交易、家族、労働、傷害、専門職責任を扱います。Aは可視性と理解、Bは規範と実務を混同し、Dは身分差を否定します。

questions.prompt: Which additional evidence does the passage recommend for investigating actual legal practice?

options.label: A
options.text: Contracts, letters, court records, and archaeological evidence compared with the monument

options.label: B
options.text: The monument alone, treated as a complete record of every dispute

options.label: C
options.text: Only the image above the inscription

options.label: D
options.text: Modern statute books without ancient contextual evidence

questions.answer: 正解：A。契約、書簡、裁判記録、考古資料を突き合わせ、規範が適用・交渉・不適用となった実態を調べます。B～Dは比較史料を欠きます。

questions.prompt: What does “The text made social hierarchy legible as well as regulated conflict within it” mean?

options.label: A
options.text: The text made existing status distinctions visible and regulated disputes inside that hierarchy.

options.label: B
options.text: The text abolished the hierarchy before resolving any disputes.

options.label: C
options.text: The phrase “within it” refers to the stone monument rather than social hierarchy.

options.label: D
options.text: The text concealed every difference in legal consequence.

questions.answer: 正解：A。文書は既存の社会階層を読み取れる形にし、その階層内部の紛争を規律しました。within itはsocial hierarchyを指します。B～Dは指示対象と内容を誤ります。

questions.prompt: Which statement best corrects the claim that public inscription created the modern rule of law in ancient Babylonia?

options.label: A
options.text: Display was significant, but it did not guarantee literacy, equal status, independent courts, or consistent enforcement; the monument must be compared with records of practice.

options.label: B
options.text: Public display proves universal literacy and identical rights for every status and gender.

options.label: C
options.text: Because the text is visible, contracts and court records cannot add evidence.

options.label: D
options.text: The monument has no legal or historical value at all.

questions.answer: 正解：A。公開の意義を認めつつ、識字、平等、独立司法、一貫した執行を自動的に証明しないため実務史料が必要です。B・Cは過大評価、Dは価値を全面否定します。
